text:
ConocoPhillips fell just barely today, after climbing nearly 5.5% over the past two weeks. The tiny decline comes amid major geopolitical shifts: Trump has struck a deal to import Russian diesel into U.S. and global markets to ease fuel prices, and is signaling a potential "energy ceasefire" between Russia and Ukraine. For an oil and gas producer, cheaper diesel flooding the market—especially from a previously sanctioned competitor—typically pressures margins and reduces the premium for domestic supply.

The broader context is that oil refineries across North America and Europe have been crippled by the wars in Eastern Europe and the Middle East, leaving the U.S. short on diesel and fuel. That supply crunch had been pushing prices higher and benefiting producers. Russian diesel entering the market directly undercuts that advantage, which likely explains why the stock paused its recent rally despite crude prices (Brent at $125) remaining elevated.
